content.text: {"label":"unknown_demand_surge","explanation":"Calls are above forecast on both queues: payments is +46% in the 15:15 interval and +18% for the day, and general is about +25–28%. On payments the rise is spread across every call reason at roughly 1.1–1.5x normal, with no single reason dominating. Supply matches plan: agents on phones equal agents planned, and no absences are logged. There are no customer-facing incidents and no marketing entries. AHT is mixed rather than consistently high. This is a demand surge with no identified cause.","plan_name":"Payments surge recovery with general top-up, 15:30-20:00","rationale":"Payments is at roughly 30–54% service level, so it needs extra capacity. Cross-skilled moves are not possible because general is itself at 60–70% and must stay at or above 70% to donate. The plan therefore uses the free levers on payments: delaying breaks that are not yet covered by this morning's delay, and cancelling remaining coaching. It adds staggered overtime as the main new capacity. Committed overtime spend is about Rs 4,320 from this morning, and the new offers add about Rs 5,470, keeping the day near Rs 9,800, inside the Rs 15,000 budget. Chat deflection takes status-type contacts off payments, and a callback offer runs until 18:00 so returned work lands in the later overtime window. General also gets a smaller overtime offer and chat deflection on balance enquiries to protect its service
